name: rgllm/awesome-portugal-data
what_it_holds: Curated awesome-list (512 stars, ~476 linked resources) of Portuguese open-data sources. Directly links: INE Portugal's official statistics API (https://www.ine.pt/xportal/xmain?xpid=INE&xpgid=ine_api), Turismo de Portugal's open-data portal (https://dadosabertos.turismodeportugal.pt/), the national tourism enterprise registry (https://registos.turismodeportugal.pt/), and Pordata municipal/EU statistics (https://www.pordata.pt/).
why_useful: One-stop index confirming Portugal's national tourism statistics office (INE) has a documented, token-free REST/webservice API, and that Turismo de Portugal runs its own open-data portal — both plausible sources for Portugal-specific nights/occupancy series feeding the EMEA regional split. The repo itself holds no data, just curated links.

name: dnme-minturdep/turismo_internacional
what_it_holds: R Shiny dashboard from Argentina's national Ministry of Tourism statistics directorate (DNMyE) covering international inbound/outbound tourism flows and the tourism trade balance across transport modes (SINTA system). Likely bundles source CSVs feeding the dashboard (typical for these Shiny repos), though exact files not confirmed from the listing alone.
why_useful: Off-Europe but hits gap 7 directly (LatAm regional travel volume, Argentina named explicitly): an official national-ministry GitHub with programmatically-built international tourism series, maintained by the same DNMyE org that also runs 'armonizacion' (harmonization of provincial tourism stats) and 'calendario_dnmye' (a SINTA release calendar — useful for point-in-time release-date tracking, gap 4).

name: fixed-effects-panel-ols-covid-impact-on-amtrak-ridership
what_it_holds: Fixed-effects panel-OLS study of COVID's impact on Amtrak ridership; repo built/updated as recently as June 2026, MIT licensed, likely includes a route/state-level panel spanning pre- and post-COVID years (needs a contents check to confirm exact vintage and whether data is route-level or system-level).
why_useful: If the panel is route- or state-level and covers 2019-2025+, it would be the freshest/most granular Amtrak series found and could proxy regional US ground-travel recovery relevant to domestic leisure travel demand (gap #10); worth a directory-listing check before relying on it.
themes: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi

name: nyc-taxi-pipeline
what_it_holds: ELT pipeline (PySpark/dbt/Airflow/DuckDB/Metabase) built against the official NYC TLC Trip Record data (data.cityofnewyork.us / TLC), which includes airport pickup/dropoff flags (JFK/LGA/EWR) by taxi zone, 2009-present monthly Parquet files. Repo itself is boilerplate with no committed rows.
why_useful: Representative of dozens of near-identical NYC TLC ETL-pipeline repos found in this search; none add unique data, but they collectively confirm the TLC Trip Record Parquet archive (with an airport-trip flag) is the standing free, monthly, decade-plus, one-command-pullable source for gap #10's NYC airport-taxi-trips ask -- worth pulling directly from the TLC site rather than via any of these repos.

name: chicago-taxi-data
what_it_holds: Scripts to download and analyze City of Chicago taxi trip records (~200M rows as of Q1 2020) and Transportation Network Provider/TNP data (Uber/Lyft, ~130M rows), plus census-tract/community-area mapping, weather data, and shapefiles. Data pulled from Chicago's open-data portal (70GB+ CSV), not committed.
why_useful: Second major US metro ground-travel/rideshare volume series for gap #10; Chicago is a top-10 US market with international airport connections (O'Hare), useful as a cross-check on the NYC TLC series for broader US travel-demand read-through.
